AI NEWS BRIEFING — 08 Nov 2026

TOP STORY
Moonshot published the full weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro: 2.8 trillion parameters, 1M-token context, 1.56 TB download. It scores 65.7 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 66.4 for Claude Opus 5.5, and 55 on Artificial Analysis's index — the highest an open-weight model has reached. Largest open-weight release to date.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816B open-weight agent model, with hosted APIs on Baseten, Fireworks, Groq, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together; Baidu open-sourced a 280B base model with no post-training.
2. Anthropic is pushing a pre-Thanksgiving IPO at $1.25–1.75 trillion, below the $2 trillion some investors wanted; OpenAI closed $11B at a $1.25 trillion valuation.
3. Google DeepMind says supervised AI agents found two new weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA — a claimed 1,600x faster forgery method, theoretical and not measured end to end. RSA-2048 is unaffected.
4. Google bought Crusoe's unfinished Wyoming data centre site and plans $17B there; Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is GA with 15-second clips at about $0.07/sec for 720p.
5. METR estimates Anthropic's capability gains are running about 1.9x faster, ~80% from AI-assisted research — but Anthropic redacted most of the evidence. Microsoft also shipped APM, a package manager for agent skills and MCP servers.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY — The Verification Gap
Every headline number this week arrived with an asterisk about who checked it: theoretical cryptanalysis multipliers, a partly redacted independent audit, and vendor-run benchmarks behind the open-weight releases. The capability is real; the measurement layer has not kept up.

Full briefing: https://dilip457.github.io/ai-news-daily/
